transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-30 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Tom Herrera (SE), Lena Wu (CS) — Evan Chung (CTO), Priya Nair (Platform Lead), Diego Ramos (SRE), Marta Iverson (PM)

Auto Summary (auto-generated): Discussed reserved GPU commitments for POC, burst capacity options, fallback strategy (model variant & region), and benchmark plans. Action items and next steps captured.

[00:00] Aisha: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — quick intro from my side, I'm Aisha, I'll run point for the POC and coordinate. Tom will dive into the sizing bits.
[00:22] Evan: Hey Aisha, Evan here. We're excited, we need clarity on how reserved GPUs vs hosted works for short spikes, and what fallback looks like if we hit limits.
[00:36] Tom: Cool, quick caveat, I'll say the numbers are ballpark until we see your token distribution and concurrency but we can scope a safe reserve.
[01:05] Priya: Our main goals — p99 latency under 300ms for the assistant route, cost predictable month-over-month, and no data egress for sensitive calls (VPC required).
[01:40] Aisha: Noted. VPC + KMS for keys, we have a Private option; for the POC most customers do Redwood Dedicated reserved pool with burst capacity enabled.
[02:14] Diego: When you say burst, is that on the same GPUs or do you spin up extra instances in a different region? We need to understand failover timing.
[02:45] Tom: Good q. We do reserved GPU pools in your chosen region; burst can use short-lived burst nodes in the same AZ or cross-region depending on policy. Typical warm-up is ~30-90s for a new node depending on image and model size.
[03:20] Marta: Is there an autoscale queue? We worry about request tails causing big cost spikes.
[03:45] Tom: Yes, we support request queueing + concurrency limits. You can configure soft queuing thresholds, and we have fallback to model-variant when queue exceeds X. E.g., switch from 13B fp16 to a 6B quantized variant for non-critical inference.
[04:30] Evan: That quantized model variant — what's the perf delta and how do we evaluate quality regressions?
[04:55] Tom: Typically 5-12% quality delta depending on task; we'll run eval suites. We'll tie quality regression alerts to your prompt set so we only fallback when tolerable.
[05:30] Priya: On security — SOC2 and audit logs, SAML SSO for console, and KMS integration for key control. We need to see compliance docs.
[05:55] Aisha: We'll share our security pack (SOC2 report, data flow diagrams, SAML guide) after the call — link in notes.
[06:30] Priya: Great. Let's talk sizing: our baseline is 1.2k RPS (requests per second) average across 2 routes with 2.1 tokens avg per call, and spikes up to 6k RPS during product launches. Token distribution attached in the doc.
[07:05] Tom: Rough calc, assuming 2.1 tokens per response seems low? Is that request+response or response only?
[07:30] Evan: Sorry, that's response tokens average. Full round trip ~8 tokens.
[07:55] Tom: Ok, that changes things. With 8 tokens per request and target latency ~300ms p99 we can sketch concurrency needs. For 6k RPS sustained spike we need about ~6k concurrent tokens per second. With batching and KV cache we can reduce GPU utilization.
[08:40] Aisha: We'll propose a reserved baseline sized for your 95th percentile day and enable burst to cover short 10-15 minute spikes. For longer sustained spikes we recommend increasing reserved ahead of major launches.
[09:12] Marta: What are typical autoscale cooldowns? We don't want flapping.
[09:35] Tom: Autoscale policies can have a cooldown of 5-10 minutes; we also have hysteresis based on moving averages. For POC we usually set conservative cooldowns to avoid thrash.
[10:00] Diego: If burst fails or we run out of capacity, what's fallback?
[10:22] Tom: Two-layer fallback: 1) Local queueing and graceful degradation (e.g., short answers), 2) Automatic model variant fallback to cheaper/quantized models, 3) Region failover as last resort. We can configure priority: cheap-model-first for non-user-facing metadata routes, preserve full-quality for critical routes.
[11:05] Evan: Region failover — latency impact? Our users are US-only, so regional fallback to close-by region acceptable but still expect bump.
[11:30] Tom: Expect extra ~50-120ms depending on region; we'll measure during bench runs.
[12:05] Priya: Okay benchmarks. What do you need from us to run a representative test?
[12:30] Aisha: We need 1-week traffic trace (timestamps, route names, token counts), sample prompt set, and target success criteria (latency percentile, throughput, error rate).
[12:50] Priya: We'll send the trace and sample prompts by end of week.
[13:10] Tom: For the POC bench we'll run three phases: smoke (single node, sanity), scale (ramp to 2x expected traffic), and spike (simulate your launch pattern with step traffic). We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tail latencies, token throughput, and cost per 1M tokens under both reserved and burst.
[13:55] Marta: How do you compute cost — is burst billed per-second or per-minute and how are reserved commitments amortized?
[14:20] Aisha: Burst is billed per-second with a short min charge; reserved capacity is monthly commit amortized daily. We'll include a sample amortization sheet.
[14:50] Diego: Any guardrails for expensive calls? We have an embedding route that's heavy — can we route that to a separate SKU?
[15:10] Tom: Yes route-based policies are supported. You can pin routes to different model sizes/instances. That also lets you isolate embeddings to non-peak pools.
[15:40] Evan: For the POC timeframe, what's realistic timeline? We need results before our Q4 launch (mid-Sept).
[16:05] Aisha: If you send traces by Aug 2, we can schedule bench on week of Aug 9, deliver report Aug 13, and run two optimization iterations by Aug 27 — so POC wrap mid-Sept is feasible.
[16:40] Priya: Who's the tech contact for runs?
[16:55] Tom: I'll be the bench owner, Tom Herrera. We'll create a runbook and share a slack channel.
[17:20] Marta: Let's talk success criteria — we want p99 < 300ms and cost per active MAU below X (we'll give exact target).
[17:47] Aisha: We'll include a success criteria doc template. For p99 target we'll test under your spike profile; if quantized fallback violates SLAs we'll mark that route as non-fallback.
[18:20] Diego: Any limitations on model sizes for burst nodes? Large 70B models take much longer to spin up.
[18:45] Tom: Correct — large models are slower to initialize. For POC recommend keeping critical routes on 7-13B classes for burst-friendly behavior; 70B should be pre-warmed on reserved if you need it.
[19:15] Evan: For storage of KV caches across restarts — what's persisted?
[19:40] Tom: We persist checkpointed KV cache for warm starts when configured; otherwise cold starts rebuild which costs latency. We'll document options.
[20:05] Priya: Who signs the reserved contract? Legal lead? We need procurement timelines.
[20:30] Aisha: We can provide a POC short-term reserved agreement; final enterprise contract later. Legal docs and procurement checklist will be in the security pack.
[21:00] Marta: Are there demo artifacts we can see?
[21:20] Aisha: Yes deck + bench spreadsheet: https://redwood.ai/poc-pack/mantle-playbook (internal link) and a benchmark runbook gist.
[22:00] Evan: Regarding monitoring — what metrics and dashboards do we get?
[22:22] Tom: Token-level cost, per-route latency, model-specific throughput, GPU utilization, queue depth, and error traces. We can add custom alerts for p99 breaches.
[23:00] Priya: Nice. On fallback quality alerts — can we set threshold to auto-revert if quality drops below X?
[23:25] Tom: Yes, automatic rollback by quality metric is supported. We'll need your evaluation harness and thresholds.
[24:10] Aisha: Quick note on costs — we'll show the delta between reserved baseline + amortized cost vs burst-billed only. Also show simulated spend if launch traffic repeats twice per month.
[24:50] Diego: Any competitor differences we should be aware of? Evan: We looked at ProdigyCloud and Vertex; they had different burst billing models and slower pre-warm times.
[25:20] Tom: We'll include a short competitive note in the POC brief.
[26:00] Marta: Alright, maybe walk us through a sample fallback run?
[26:25] Tom: Example: route A hits 95th percentile CPU spike — requests queued for 30s then overflow triggers fallback to 6B quantized model for non-critical fields while critical reply uses full model with rationing. We'll log percentage of requests served by fallback.
[27:10] Evan: How do we validate user impact? We need to compare NPS/error rates pre/post fallback.
[27:35] Aisha: We'll instrument canary cohorts and capture user-facing metrics. For POC we can run a synthetic traffic mix and a small live canary.
[28:05] Priya: About logging and retention — audit logs needed for 180 days. Is that configurable?
[28:30] Tom: Yes retention tiers exist; we can set 180 days for your account under enterprise plan.
[29:00] Marta: Anything else on network egress and data residency?
[29:25] Aisha: We can pin region and VPC; no customer data leaves the VPC in Private deployments. We'll detail network flows in the security pack.
[30:00] Evan: Good. Let's confirm the bench schedule again.
[30:20] Aisha: Bench week of Aug 9 — smoke Tue, scale Wed, spike Thu — report Friday Aug 13. We'll send calendar invites.
[31:05] Priya: We'll produce the trace by Aug 2.
[31:30] Diego: If we find that reserved + burst still exceeds budget, any mid-POC levers?
[31:55] Tom: Several: tighter batching, prefix caching, model quantization, route-specific fallbacks, and delaying non-urgent tasks to off-peak windows. We'll test these in iterations.
[32:30] Marta: Can you show an example cost savings from batching?
[32:48] Tom: Yes, one of our case studies showed batching and KV cache cut token cost by ~35% for a conversational assistant. We'll include that case study link.
[33:20] Evan: Ok recap please — what do we each own by next week?
[33:40] Aisha: Redwood: send cost spreadsheet, security pack, benchmark runbook, calendar for bench; Tom: runbook and bench nodes; Customer: traffic trace + success criteria + sign-off on bench dates.
[34:10] Priya: Confirmed.
[34:30] Marta: Logistics — do you need VPN access or do you run tests from your side?
[34:50] Tom: We'll run from Redwood infra hitting your endpoints through VPC peering; we may need temporary creds and an allowlist. We'll share the exact access steps.
[35:20] Evan: Great. Any open concerns?
[35:40] Priya: Only that we need a clear rollback plan if fallback causes bad regressions.
[36:00] Tom: We'll include rollback steps and monitor windows.
[36:30] Aisha: Alright let's wrap. Thanks everyone.
[36:45] Evan: Thanks.
[37:05] Marta: Thanks, talk soon.

Action recap (verbatim):
- Aisha to share cost model + security pack + deck (link) by 2027-08-03.
- Tom to prepare benchmark runbook and GPU matrix by 2027-08-05.
- Priya to share 1-week traffic trace and sample prompts by 2027-08-02.
- Schedule bench week of 2027-08-09.

End of transcript.
